reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must accept FUNCTION VARIANCE followed by a parenthesised list of one or more argument-1 (identifier, literal, arithmetic expression, or a table reference with ALL subscripts since the format repeats the argument, §1989:A.2.2), separated by spaces, commas or semicolons, used only in an arithmetic expression, and refuse a list of zero arguments, the bare name, and an empty '( )'.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 window: sig.IntroducedIn (85 on this row) against ctx.Edition.DialectLevel, COBOL1502 below it
construct function-empty-argument-list-2002: an empty '( )' after the name draws COBOL0900 below 2002 (the 1985 format braces argument-1 inside the parentheses)
construct NumericFunctionIdentifierOperand2002: a numeric function written where an identifier stands (MOVE sender) draws COBOL0900 below 2002 (§1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4)
construct RepositoryFunction2002: below 2002 a name written without FUNCTION is never read as a function (it binds as a data reference, COBOL1639); at 2023 it draws COBOL1543
FUNCTION is reserved at r85 (true at every edition)

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 an empty '( )' argument list is refused by COBOL0900 before the arity check, a numeric function-identifier as a MOVE/identifier operand is refused (2002 Annex F.2 item 60 lifted it), and the keyword-omitted form is not a function reference; at 2023 those take the later arms. The accepted forms and the arity check (COBOL1504) are the same code at every edition

reader.notes: The catalog row VARIANCE (Variadic, 1..inf, IntroducedIn 85) drives the generic argument path; arity is checked in BindFunctionResult over the written arguments with an ALL table counted as its elements. The format citation §1989:A.2.45.2 itself cannot pass cite.py (its quotation has only 3 real words), so the description clause and the function-identifier format are cited instead.
